title: Redirect Trilogy
story: Every Linux process has three standard streams: `stdin` (0), `stdout` (1), and `stderr` (2). Noisy programs often mix status messages and decoys across `stdout` and `stderr`. Master `>`, `>>`, `2>`, and `/dev/null` to capture what matters.
objective:
Complete all three stages, then run `quest check`:
1. Stage 1 (`>`): Run `/challenge/run > ~/myflag` to redirect `stdout` into `~/myflag` while `stderr` still prints on your terminal.
2. Stage 2 (`>` and `>>`): Run `/challenge/run --part1 > ~/twopart.txt` and then `/challenge/run --part2 >> ~/twopart.txt` to append the second half without overwriting the first.
3. Stage 3 (`2>` and `/dev/null`): `/challenge/run2` prints decoy lines on `stdout` and the real Stage 3 token on `stderr`. Redirect `stderr` into `~/stderr_flag.txt` (`2> ~/stderr_flag.txt`) and silence `stdout` (`> /dev/null`).
4. Run `quest check` to claim your `CYBERUS{...}` flag!
hints: `>` redirects `stdout` (stream 1) to a file (overwriting it); `>>` appends `stdout` to the end of a file.
`2> file` redirects `stderr` (stream 2) to `file`. Note: `2>&1` merges `stderr` into wherever `stdout` points, whereas `2> file` captures ONLY `stderr`!
